title: Atomic policy evaluation race leading to region and tier mismatches during high load
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Summary: During several customer escalations last week we observed large batches of requests being routed to incorrect region/tier/model variants for ~90s windows under sustained load. The visible effects were: increased latency, token cost spikes, and downstream application errors when customers expected a Dedicated model variant (pinned) but received a Hosted variant from a different region. Affected customers include two enterprise tenants using Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 and a Hosted latency-sensitive beta customer in us-east-1.

Observed behavior: When policy refreshes and concurrent tenant request bursts aligned, the policy evaluation subsystem sometimes returned a stale policy fragment that had partially-applied merges. This produced an atomicity violation: requests routed by the new decision tree used region priority from the updated policy but fallback tiers from the prior policy which lacked the dedicated mapping. Net result: requests were sent cross-region to lower-tier hosted pools.

Impact window: 2026-03-03 03:12 UTC to 2026-03-03 03:24 UTC (12 minutes) and similar repeats on 2026-03-04. Escalations logged in support triage and two on-call pages.

Customer-visible symptoms: higher 95th/99th latency, token billing anomalies, Model ID mismatch errors in application logs, and elevated error rates in Rust proxy logs (routed-to-incompatible-model).
root_cause: A race condition in the policy evaluation and cache-merge path. Policy updates are applied by a background reconciler and then incrementally merged into the route-evaluation cache. Under concurrent evaluation requests the merge was not atomically swapped; evaluators could read a partially-updated policy object (region priorities updated, tier mapping still from the old policy). The code path responsible for merges attempted a lock-free patch for performance but failed to provide a read-after-write consistent view when multiple goroutines performed evaluation+merge concurrently. Additionally, a previously-introduced micro-optimization skipped a sanity-check for pinned tenant mappings when a policy checksum matched, which prevented detection of the partial state.
mitigation: Roll-forward temporary guard: 1) disabled incremental lock-free merges; switched policy cache to a single-compare-and-swap apply path (coarse-grained but safe) via feature-flag 'safe-policy-apply'. 2) Added emergency routing rule to prefer tenant's pinned mapping for any request with tenant-pin header until fix is in runtime-1.19. 3) Notified affected customers and applied manual re-routing for two tenants. Outcome: routing correctness restored; latency improved within 2 minutes after flag flip. These are stop-gap changes and have a measurable CPU cost increase on the policy reconciler.
proposed_fix: Implement an atomic policy state machine: produce fully-validated policy snapshots in the reconciler thread and replace the route-evaluation pointer with a single atomic swap (no incremental merges). Add stronger unit and stress tests: deterministic interleaving fuzz tests using the existing policy fuzzer harness, and a synthetic high-load integration test that simulates concurrent policy refreshes under production QPS. Reintroduce a lightweight checksum validation that ensures pinned tenant mappings are present in the new snapshot before swapping. Expected work: code changes in route-eval (C++/Rust layer) + reconciler (Go), tests, and benching. Estimated 8 story points. Target release in runtime-1.19 with feature flag gated rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge fix behind feature flag 'atomic-policy-swap' in runtime-1.19 branch. 2) Deploy to staging + soak for 48h with synthetic policy-change storm tests. 3) Canary rollout to 10% of traffic in us-east-1 for 2 hours, monitor routing correctness, latency, and CPU on policy reconciler. 4) Expand to Dedicated clusters in eu-west-1 and us-central-1. 5) Full rollout after 24h of stable canaries. 6) Post-deploy validation: run tenant-specific regression prompts and confirm pinned mapping enforcement. Backout plan: flip feature flag off to return to safe-policy-apply and contact on-call if anomalies detected.
postmortem_actions:
- Ship atomic-policy-swap fix and remove emergency switch in 2 weeks.
- Add invariants to policy reconciler: assert pinned-mapping presence on snapshot creation.
- Add telemetry: gauge for policy-snapshot-age, counter for partial-merge-detections, and alert when evaluation sees mismatched checksums.
- Incorporate policy-evaluation race scenarios into chaos testbed.
- Run tabletop with SRE and Support to improve customer communication playbook for routing incidents.
- Update runbook: add step to flip safe-policy-apply and manual tenant re-route checklist.
- Schedule post-release performance review to tune reconciler CPU cost.
